summary: Presigned artifact fetch failures: VPCE path rewrites Host -> 307 redirect to internal-only hostname
description: Issue summary: Customer reported that model artifact downloads (presigned S3 URLs) and control-plane asset fetches intermittently fail with 403/connection errors. Impact: multiple serving nodes in Acme Health private deployment failing to fetch large model shards during rolling updates, causing degraded model availability and 5xx errors for in-flight inference requests. Environment: Private deployment (VPCE to Redwood control plane) over Direct Connect + partner firewall/proxy.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a model rollout that causes serving node to request presigned artifact (GET presigned url). 2) Observe HTTP client follow behavior in the customer's egress path (their proxy rewrites Host header). 3) Reproduce fetch from a serving node: curl -v --location '<presigned-url>' 4) Note: some requests receive 307 redirect with Location set to an internal-only hostname and subsequent fetch fails with 403 or DNS resolution error.
observed_behavior: Serving node receives 307 redirect pointing to an internal hostname (e.g. https://internal-s3.local.acme/...). The node cannot resolve or reach that name from the VPCE subnet, resulting in fetch failure and artifact download abort. Some nodes log 403 from S3 because the redirect changed the Host used for presigned validation.
expected_behavior: Presigned URL should return 200 with S3 object; if a redirect occurs it should point to a publicly resolvable host or preserve original presigned host so signature remains valid.
initial_hypothesis: Customer's edge proxy or VPCE endpoint is rewriting Host headers for egress traffic and/or performing a redirect translation that replaces external S3 hostnames with internal hostnames. This breaks presigned-url signature validation and/or DNS resolution for serving nodes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Support (Maya): Collected failing request logs from a serving node (node-az1-12). curl -v output shows initial 302/307 with 'Location: https://internal-s3.local.acme/awsbucket/shard?id=...'.
tcpdump from serving node shows outbound GET to presigned host, followed by immediate HTTP/1.1 307 from an intermediate proxy (10.10.5.2) altering Location header.

Sample headers captured: 'Host: s3.amazonaws.com' -> rewritten to 'Host: internal-s3.local.acme' at egress; 'X-Forwarded-For' added by proxy. Presigned signature components in query string remain for original host which no longer matches rewritten Host, causing S3 to return 403 when followed without preserving original host header.
Checked VPCE configuration: endpoint policy allowed S3 object GETs. VPC route table shows traffic to VPCE egress going through customer transit VNF chain where the rewrite is located.

Customer confirmed they have a 'host rewrite for compliance' rule on their outbound proxy that maps external S3 hostnames to internal-cached S3 gateway. That gateway is not reachable from the VPCE subnets used by serving nodes (split-routing).

Confirmed no code change on Redwood side triggered this; similar failures started after customer rolled out a proxy config change on 2026-03-09 (change rolled back for other services earlier but not VPCE traffic).

SRE note: We simulated follow-redirect with curl --location and observed that when Host header mismatches presigned-url host, S3 returns 403. Also validated that when we preserved original Host (curl -H 'Host: s3.amazonaws.com') the request succeeds against the presigned url despite the redirect chain.
Related runbook search: found Confluence guidance for VPCE egress and host rewrite pitfalls (linked).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:04 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage complete. Asked customer to provide example presigned URL and a PCAP. Customer reply attached pcap and proxy config snippet showing rewrite rules.

2026-03-10 13:30 UTC - Customer (Acme Network Team, Raj Patel): We enabled a host-rewrite to route S3 traffic to an internal caching gateway for audit/cost reasons. That gateway returns 307s to internal hostnames. We did not realize VPCE subnets are not part of our internal DNS zone.

2026-03-10 15:12 UTC - Liam O'Neill (SRE): Reproduced locally using a container leaving Host header intact vs rewritten. Presigned validation fails when Host is replaced. Recommend customer preserve Host or allow VPCE CIDR to resolve internal gateway names (not ideal).
2026-03-11 08:45 UTC - Raj Patel (Acme): We've disabled the host-rewrite rule for VPCE CIDR. Observing artifact fetch retries now succeed for nodes that reattempted. Will monitor for next 24h.

2026-03-12 09:05 UTC - Liam O'Neill (SRE): Confirmed customer rollback fixed the immediate issue. Added note to implement client-side guard in SDK to refuse redirects that change hostname away from presigned host (security).
2026-03-12 16:00 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Closing ticket after monitoring window. Follow-ups: create runbook and SDK safe-redirect PR.
resolution: Workaround/fix: Customer disabled the host-rewrite rule for VPCE CIDR and/or configured their egress gateway to preserve the original Host header on HTTP redirects for presigned S3 flows. Redwood actions: added a defensive check in runtime SDK (PR linked) to refuse to follow redirects that change the presigned URL's hostname without explicit opt-in, and added VPCE egress validation steps to our runbook. Rollout: SDK change merged and staged to Canary on 2026-03-11, full rollout 2026-03-12. Follow-ups: (1) Confluence runbook updated with detection steps and recommended customer config; (2) Ask Solutions Engineering to surface VPCE host-preservation requirement in onboarding checklist.
resolution_notes: Customer confirmed all failing nodes recovered after the host-rewrite rollback and a small number of in-progress downloads had to be re-triggered manually.
Deployed runtime/SDK defensive behavior to refuse unsafe hostname redirects to prevent silent signature breakage in the future (related PR applied to 1.3.x and main).
Created runbook: 'VPCE egress host rewrite - detection and remediation' and added to Private Deployment onboarding checklist.
Postmortem: No SLA breach. Action items assigned: SE to update onboarding (AC-12), SRE to add automated alert for repeated 307->403 patterns from serving nodes (SRE-457).
